clue.text: Avoid times to die

parts.note: times as in multiplication, two by three
to pass, or pass away, is to die

explanation.surface: Advice on cheating death, or a grim remark about avoiding the times when people die.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round something rather than through it is to skirt or avoid it.

clue.text: City bankrupt as lawyer exercises intervention

indicators.note: intervention means coming between, so these pieces sit inside the bankrupt word

parts.note: bust means bankrupt
a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
PE is physical education, exercises at school

explanation.surface: A bankrupt lawyer's workout gets an intervention.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Hungary, on the Danube, is a city.

clue.text: Cheap books to destroy if pupil not about

indicators.note: destroying the words breaks them apart so their letters can be rebuilt

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Teachers telling a pupil to destroy cheap books if not about to read them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to destroy' mixes IF PUPIL NOT with C. Also the Tarantino film, one of this puzzle's films.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid fiction printed on cheap wood-pulp paper gave the genre its name: cheap, sensational books.

clue.text: Second kind of lawyer

parts.note: ilk means kind or sort

explanation.surface: Another kind of lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a senior barrister, a King's Counsel, wears a gown of the material and is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A King's Counsel is informally named after the fabric of the gown, so a senior lawyer.

clue.text: Hairstyle to test out in court

indicators.note: the hairstyle's letters are set in the middle of the test's letters

parts.note: a trial is a test, a try-out
a bun is a hairstyle with the hair coiled at the back

explanation.surface: A judge trying out a new hairdo in the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A judicial body hearing cases is a court; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Anger about director on hospital department's mockery

indicators.note: about means around, so the anger word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to rile is to anger

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: the ICU is the intensive care unit of a hospital

explanation.surface: Anger at a director meddling in the hospital department invites ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: Derision, making fun of someone, is mockery.

clue.text: Sad to arrest worker

definitions.note: the adjective describes manual workers; here it stands for such a worker

parts.note: blue means sad, low
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A sorry business: police having to arrest a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual workers wore blue overalls, so the term describes a manual or industrial labourer.

clue.text: African runner loses footing and gets nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river, a runner being something that runs

explanation.surface: An African athlete slips, falls, and wins nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a crossword word for river, here the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a sports score of zero, meaning nothing.

clue.text: Despicable creep imprisons independent woman

indicators.note: imprisons means holds inside, so the letter goes within the creep's letters

parts.note: a louse is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A vile creep holds an independent woman captive.
explanation.walkthrough: With 22 down she is the other half of the film Thelma & Louise.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, French in origin, so any woman so called.

clue.text: Place to stay after golf

definitions.meaning: an inn or lodging house for travellers
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for H follows Golf

explanation.surface: Booking a room after a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodging for guests is a place to stay, and the same word is the phonetic code for H, which follows G.

clue.text: Playwright drunk inspires a couple of lines on the way back

indicators.note: heading back means the whole assembled string is read right to left
to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the drunk word takes the lines inside it

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: A drunken playwright breathes life into a couple of lines on his way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspires' is used literally, breathing in, so the lines are taken inside before the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Don DeLillo, the American novelist, also wrote stage plays such as The Day Room.

clue.text: Former president's party joined by confused university Blue

definitions.note: the president's letter: George W. Bush's middle initial, nicknamed Dubya, written out in full

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Blue (an Oxbridge sporting honour) turns up muddled at an ex-president's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns BLUE into BLEU. The definition is the president's initial: George W. Bush was nicknamed Dubya.
explanation.definitionFit: George W. Bush's middle initial gave his nickname, so the letter's spelt-out name stands for that former president's initial.

clue.text: Dragon breath

definitions.meaning: the Magic Dragon of the Peter, Paul and Mary song
a short breath or gust of air, as in a whiff of smoke

explanation.surface: A dragon's fiery breath.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's dragon is named after a short gust, which is also a small breath of air.

clue.text: Vacating place service affected small demonstrations

indicators.note: vacating empties the word place, leaving just its outer letters

parts.note: an ace is an unreturned tennis service
camp means theatrically affected or mannered

explanation.surface: A church service turned stagey when the congregation left, producing only small protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacating place' leaves PL's outer pair, P and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Protest encampments, like the women's one at Greenham Common, are long-running demonstrations against weapons or war.

clue.text: Implies boxes possibly restrict temperature in rough city area

parts.note: means means implies

indicators.note: restrict means hem in, so the trees' letters go round the temperature letter

parts.note: box is a kind of tree, so boxes are possibly trees

explanation.surface: Packaging that implies a tight limit on temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers but is the shrub, an example of trees, so 'possibly' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Also Scorsese's film: the phrase means a tough, dangerous urban neighbourhood.

clue.text: He'll transport one down to the Thames, perhaps under stress

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces under the stress word come below it

parts.note: to tax is to strain or stress
I is the Roman numeral one
the Thames is an example of a river

explanation.surface: A stressed passenger heads down to the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab driver's job is to transport passengers.

clue.text: Spies infiltrate very liberal party

indicators.note: spies infiltrating get inside, so the agency's letters go within the other pieces

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents penetrate a very liberal political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering for fun, a get-together, is a party.

clue.text: Fatefully compromised trade union leaves blank sheet

indicators.note: compromised means damaged or corrupted, so the remaining letters are rearranged
leaves means goes away from, so these letters are taken out of the word

explanation.surface: A union leader quits after a fatal compromise, leaving a blank sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes T and U out of FATEFULLY, leaving FAEFLLY; 'compromised' mixes those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank page at the front or back of a book, attached to the cover, is that sheet.

clue.text: German detective gutted, upsetting French cop

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disordering, so the letters are rearranged
gutted means emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A German detective, crushed, upsets a French policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves DE from 'detective'; 'upsetting' mixes GERMAN and DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the French national police force is the classic French cop.

clue.text: What to play in hot pea soup

indicators.note: soup suggests a jumbled mixture, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for performing in a cafe while serving hot pea soup.
explanation.definitionFit: The keyboard instrument is something one plays, so it answers what to play.

clue.text: Small child wearing hat in short supply

indicators.note: the child is inside the hat, so the hat's letters surround it

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child in a hat, and hats are scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are restricted are scarce, in short supply.

clue.text: First month at school for folk guitarist

parts.note: January, abbreviated Jan, is the first month

explanation.surface: A young folk guitarist's first month at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Bert Jansch was a Scottish folk guitarist, a founder of Pentangle.

clue.text: Woman covering her head with strange metal

indicators.note: covering means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the other letter
strange signals the letters are made odd, rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A woman wears a headdress of strange metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns METAL to TELMA, wrapped round H from 'her head'. With 8 down she makes the film Thelma & Louise.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so any woman so called.

clue.text: Imposing, with old king on top

indicators.note: in a down clue the king piece sits on top, coming first

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: An imposing figure with an old king above him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something splendid and impressive in size or style is imposing.

clue.text: Medieval local officials who scored centuries?

definitions.meaning: officers of a hundred, the medieval English subdivision of a shire
jokingly, people who scored hundreds, as a batter making a century of runs in cricket

explanation.surface: Old officials who, it seems, racked up hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: A century in cricket is 100 runs scored by one batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundred was a county subdivision with its own court, run by officials named for it.

clue.text: German almost ready to eat bag

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: fruit that is ripe is ready to eat

explanation.surface: A German nearly ready to tuck into a bag of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling bag or holdall is also called by this name, especially in American use.

clue.text: Book in prompt 27?

definitions.note: the number 27 is three times three times three, an example of such a power

indicators.note: the book letter is placed inside the prompt word

parts.note: a cue is a prompt to an actor

explanation.surface: Is there a book in prompt 27, a cross-reference to another clue?
explanation.walkthrough: 27 looks like a cross-reference to 27 across, but it is just the number, three to the power three; the question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Three multiplied by itself three times gives 27, the third power of three.

clue.text: Pause journey, very excited initially to be in Return of the King

indicators.note: the initial letters are to be placed inside the reversed word
return means the word for kingly is read backwards

parts.note: royal means of or belonging to the king

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: A very excited fan breaks a journey to see Return of the King, the Lord of the Rings film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns ROYAL into LAYOR, and V and E from 'very excited initially' go in before the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a break in a journey, so to make one is to pause it.

clue.text: Sure your electric Skoda starts?

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Checking whether someone's electric Skoda will start.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure, as a reply, is an affirmative, agreeing.

clue.text: One of us oddly missing that people are things in themselves according to Kant

definitions.text: things in themselves according to Kant

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of these words are dropped, keeping the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: men are people
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

explanation.surface: A puzzling philosophical remark about one of us vanishing, and people as Kant's things in themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: From ONEOFUS the even letters N, O, U remain. 'are' gives A, the symbol for the area unit of 100 square metres; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kant's term for things as they are in themselves, apart from how they appear to the senses, is the plural of noumenon.

clue.text: Engrossed by choice between muscles and a teaching qualification

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
or presents a choice between alternatives
a BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: Someone engrossed in choosing between a gym body and a teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To be engrossed is to be wholly taken up with something, deeply engaged.

clue.text: We should start releases

definitions.meaning: an exhortation to begin, come on, let us begin
frees or lets loose, as in loosening a grip

explanation.surface: A call to begin the releases.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an urging to set off and, read as a verb, the act of freeing one's hold.
